faq: Which sources can you import from?

CSV and Excel files, supplier feeds, Google Sheets and exports from Shopify, WooCommerce, BigCommerce, Wix and others. If your source is unusual, send a sample first and we confirm what is possible before you order.
Can you scrape another website's products for me?
No. We only move data you own or have the right to use, such as your own old store or a supplier file you are allowed to use. We do not copy other stores' content or images.
This service covers products and their data. Customers and order history are a separate migration job, which we can quote on request, because the rules and risks are different.
What if some products fail to import?
We expect a few. Each failure is listed with the reason, such as a missing price or a duplicate handle. We fix what we can and send you a short list of items that need your input.
desc:
Product data import and migration moves your products from a spreadsheet, a supplier file or another store into your new one. Ecom Swift LLC maps each column to the right field, tests a small batch, runs the full import and checks the result against the source.

## What is a product data import?

A product data import takes product information stored somewhere else and creates product records in your store. The source might be a spreadsheet you have kept for years, a CSV file from a supplier, an export from another platform or a set of product pages on a store you are leaving. Each row becomes a product or a variant, with its title, description, price, stock, images, tags and category.

Done well, an import saves days of typing. Done badly, it creates hundreds of broken records that take longer to repair than to type from scratch.

## Why imports fail without careful mapping

Platforms disagree about how products are structured. One system puts every size on its own row, another stores sizes as options inside one product. Prices may carry currency symbols, descriptions may hold stray formatting, and image links may point to files that no longer exist.

If these differences are not handled before the import, you get duplicate products, variants stuck under the wrong parent, missing images and prices that read as zero. A mapping step, where each source column is matched to the correct destination field, is the single most valuable part of the job.

## How a good import affects your store

A correct import makes your store ready to sell on day one. Customers see complete product pages instead of half-filled ones, and you do not spend your launch week fixing data. When you are moving from another platform, a careful import also protects search visibility, because old addresses can be redirected to the new product pages instead of returning an error.

Imported data also feeds everything else. Collections, filters, search, shopping feeds and email product blocks all rely on the same fields. Correct data in means those features work properly from the start.

## What a careful import covers

- A review of the source file to find gaps, duplicates and odd formats.
- A mapping sheet linking each source column to a store field.
- Clean-up of prices, units, stock numbers and text before import.
- Handling of variants and options so sizes and colors group under one product.
- Image links downloaded and attached to the right products and variants.
- Categories, product types and tags mapped to your store's structure.
- A small test batch imported and inspected before the full run.
- A comparison of the finished store against the source.
- A list of rows that could not be moved, with the reason for each.
- A reusable import template for future batches.

## How we do it

You send the source: a file, a supplier sheet or access to the old store. We read it, list the fields it contains and prepare the mapping sheet for your review. Then we clean the data and import ten or so products as a test. You look at them, we adjust, and then we run the full import.

The Basic package suits one source file with a modest number of products and a clear import report. Standard adds variants, images and category mapping and a check against the source. Premium handles a full move from another store, with up to two sources, old addresses mapped and redirected, a reusable template and a final reconciliation sheet.

We only import data you own or have the right to use. We do not copy products from other people's websites.

## Do and avoid

**Do:**
- Keep the original source file untouched as a reference.
- Give every product a unique SKU or handle in the source.
- Decide how you want variants named before the import.
- Check the test batch on a phone and a computer.

**Avoid:**
- Importing the full file before any test.
- Mixing price formats and currencies in one column.
- Linking to images hosted on a supplier server that may disappear.
- Importing over live products without a backup.

## Who this service is for

It suits a new store owner who has a large product list in a spreadsheet and does not want to type it all. It suits a retailer switching platforms who needs products, variants and old address redirects carried over. It also suits a reseller whose supplier sends regular price and stock files.

## What we need from you

Send the source file or give us a way to export it, plus a note about any fields that need special treatment. We ask for collaborator or staff access to the destination store and never for passwords. If you are leaving an old store, tell us which products, if any, should be left behind.
